prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Restaurant Dinner Menu (language en).
Grid: 4 columns × 9 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "Starters" spans 4 col × 1 row; "Mains" spans 4 col × 1 row; "Desserts" spans 4 col × 1 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Dish" · longest unbreakable word 77px · one-line width 164px
  col 2: header "Description" · longest unbreakable word 83px · one-line width 558px
  col 3: header "Price" · longest unbreakable word 37px · one-line width 37px
  col 4: header "Allergens" · longest unbreakable word 70px · one-line width 298px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Help diners choose dishes by comparing descriptions, prices and allergens within each course.","reading":"Readers scan course headings and dish names, then read across each row for ingredients, price and allergens. Wrapped descriptions can create row height that also accommodates wrapped dish names or allergen lists.","groups":["Dish and Description belong together as the name and explanation of each menu item.","Price and Allergens are compact decision aids read alongside each dish."],"keep_intact":["Individual dish-name and ingredient words where possible.","Each price as a single value.","Allergen names where possible, so they remain easy to identify."],"may_wrap":["Dish names between words.","Descriptions at natural word boundaries.","Allergen lists between entries or words."]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r2A: widths [98, 112, 58, 91] · table 360×1071px · row heights [36, 36, 199, 176, 36, 176, 176, 36, 199] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 8 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2B: widths [98, 114, 56, 91] · table 360×1071px · row heights [60, 36, 199, 176, 36, 176, 153, 36, 199] · column headers wrapped 1/4 · tallest cell 8 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2C: widths [101, 109, 58, 91] · table 360×1095px · row heights [36, 36, 199, 176, 36, 199, 176, 36, 199] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 8 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
